name: Michael Bailey
role: Senior Advisor, AI at J-PAL, MIT; computational social scientist and economist
bio:
I'm a computational social scientist working on the intersection of AI and social good at [J-PAL](https://www.povertyactionlab.org/) (MIT). Our major initiative is the [Project on AI and Evidence (PAIE)](https://www.povertyactionlab.org/initiative/project-ai-evidence-paie) for identifying, evaluating, and scaling applications of AI for social good and in the fight against poverty, across education, health, labor markets, climate change, and financial inclusion. Previously founded the Social Capital Lab at Facebook measuring how social connection shapes economic opportunity and well-being. The Social Capital Lab produced several open datasets and research papers measuring social connectedness, social capital, and migration for researchers and policymakers. Featured Projects ====== **[Social Capital Atlas](https://www.socialcapital.org)** — Mapping social capital across U.S. communities, with public data covering nearly every ZIP code, high school, and college. **Data:** [Social Capital Atlas](https://www.socialcapital.org)
**Research:** [Nature I](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-022-04996-4) · [Nature II](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-022-04997-3)
**Media Coverage:** [New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2022/08/01/upshot/rich-poor-friendships.html) · [The Economist](https://www.economist.com/finance-and-economics/2022/08/04/why-having-rich-friends-is-good-for-you) **[Social Connectedness Index](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/social-connectedness-index)** — A publicly available measure of social connectedness between geographies, used widely to study migration, trade, COVID-19, and inequality. **Data:** [Social Connectedness Index data](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/social-connectedness-index)
**Map:** [Interactive explorer](/sci-map/) — countries, EU regions (NUTS-2), US states
**Research:** [JPE 2018](https://doi.org/10.1086/700073) · [RES 2019](https://doi.org/10.1093/restud/rdy068) · [JEP 2018](https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/jep.32.3.259)
**Media Coverage:** [New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2018/09/19/upshot/facebook-county-friendships.html) · [The Economist](https://www.economist.com/graphic-detail/2018/08/08/far-flung-facebook-friends-may-be-good-for-your-health) · [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2017-07-25/facebook-friends-from-far-away-are-a-trait-of-rich-communities) **[Global Migration Flows](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/international-migration-flows)** — Estimates of international migration patterns derived from anonymized, aggregated platform data. **Data:** [Data on HDX](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/international-migration-flows)
**Research:** [PNAS 2025](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2409418122)
**Media Coverage:** [New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/04/17/opinion/global-migration-facebook-data.html) · [NYT interactive tool](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/04/17/opinion/global-migration-facebook-data-interactive-tool.html) Featured Publications ====== A full list is on [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=CF6_E90AAAAJ). See also the [Research](/publications/) page.

projects.title: Social Capital Atlas
projects.description:
The [Social Capital Atlas](https://www.socialcapital.org) is a public dataset and interactive tool measuring three forms of social capital — economic connectedness, social cohesion, and civic engagement — across nearly every U.S. ZIP code, high school, and college. The underlying research showed that economic connectedness is one of the strongest community-level predictors of upward mobility in the United States. **Data:** [Social Capital Atlas](https://www.socialcapital.org)
**Research:** [Nature I](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-022-04996-4) · [Nature II](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-022-04997-3)
**Media Coverage:** [The New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2022/08/01/upshot/rich-poor-friendships.html) · [The Economist](https://www.economist.com/finance-and-economics/2022/08/04/why-having-rich-friends-is-good-for-you)

projects.title: Global Migration Flows
projects.description:
A cross-institutional project producing estimates of international migration flows, derived from anonymized, aggregated platform data. The work powers a public dataset on the Humanitarian Data Exchange and an interactive visualization at The New York Times. **Data:** [Data on HDX](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/international-migration-flows)
**Research:** [PNAS 2025](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2409418122)
**Media Coverage:** [New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/04/17/opinion/global-migration-facebook-data.html) · [NYT interactive tool](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/04/17/opinion/global-migration-facebook-data-interactive-tool.html)

projects.title: Project on AI and Evidence (PAIE)
projects.description:
The **Project on AI and Evidence (PAIE)** is an initiative at [J-PAL](https://www.povertyactionlab.org/) at MIT that identifies, evaluates, and scales innovative applications of AI for social good and in the fight against poverty, bringing together AI adopters, tech companies, and researchers. I joined J-PAL as Senior Advisor in July 2026 to work on this portfolio across research, policy, and practice. PAIE funds rigorous research — largely randomized evaluations — on AI applications, builds practical guidance for evaluating AI-based programs, and develops capacity among researchers, governments, and NGOs. Focus sectors include education, health, labor markets, climate change, and financial inclusion. **Initiative:** [Project on AI and Evidence at J-PAL](https://www.povertyactionlab.org/initiative/project-ai-evidence-paie)
**Co-Chairs:** Joshua Blumenstock · Iqbal Dhaliwal · David Yanagizawa-Drott
**Funders:** Community Jameel · Google.org · IDRC · UK International Development · AWS

projects.title: Social Connectedness Index
projects.description:
The Social Connectedness Index (SCI) measures the relative probability of friendship between people in different locations. The dataset has been used by researchers across economics, political science, public health, and sociology to study migration, trade, the spread of COVID-19, knowledge diffusion, and inequality. **Data:** [Social Connectedness Index data](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/social-connectedness-index)
**Map:** [Interactive explorer](/sci-map/) — countries, EU regions (NUTS-2), US states
**Research:** [JPE 2018](https://doi.org/10.1086/700073) · [RES 2019](https://doi.org/10.1093/restud/rdy068) · [JEP 2018](https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/jep.32.3.259)
**Media Coverage:** [New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2018/09/19/upshot/facebook-county-friendships.html) · [The Economist](https://www.economist.com/graphic-detail/2018/08/08/far-flung-facebook-friends-may-be-good-for-your-health) · [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2017-07-25/facebook-friends-from-far-away-are-a-trait-of-rich-communities)

projects.title: UK Social Capital Atlas
projects.description:
The **UK Social Capital Atlas** maps social capital across the United Kingdom — including *economic connectedness*, the extent to which lower- and higher-income people are friends — built from the friendship networks of roughly 20 million UK adults (around six billion friendships) on Facebook. It is the UK counterpart to the US [Social Capital Atlas](https://www.socialcapital.org), produced with the [Behavioural Insights Team](https://www.bi.team/) and partners including Meta, the RSA, the Neighbourly Lab, Opportunity Insights, and Stripe Partners, with funding from the Nuffield Foundation. The work documents that children from lower-income families who grow up in more economically connected UK communities go on to earn substantially more as adults, and that shared activities and the built environment — not just geographic proximity — shape who becomes friends. **Data:** [UK Social Capital Atlas on HDX](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/uk-social-capital-atlas)
**Research:** [SocArXiv working paper](https://osf.io/preprints/socarxiv/kb7dy_v1) · [Behavioural Insights Team report](https://www.bi.team/publications/social-capital-in-the-united-kingdom/)
